od-280-s1.notes: Silvio Jr Suppa, Design trends, A&D 280 pp.3-7. Thesis: the unstoppable rise of 'no-licence' quadricycles is redefining vehicle types; the clearest sign is the upcoming Fiat Multiplina (2028), which given the Topolino's success could peak in brand visibility with four seats. Over fifteen years ago the Renault Twizy challenged the rules with two occupants in tandem; its successor Mobilize Duo keeps the raised cell set back from the wheels but adds real glass-window doors and large unpainted sections for sustainability, a 'commercial vehicle' look, aiming to stand out from scooters and cars with a less pop, more technical design. Cause of the boom (sales +13.5%): the forced elimination of the A-segment due to mandatory driver-assistance systems (2024), profit squeeze, EV investment and battery costs. Retro references dominate: Topolino and Multiplina reframe the golden age of the Fiat in miniature; the Swiss Microlino draws on the Isetta bubble car; Topolino's Verde Vivo colour and beach-inspired designs (XEV Dune) lay bare the lack of safety; Linktour Alumi uses an aluminium body and technological language; Dacia Hipster's bonnet-to-cabin proportions recall the 1959 Mini though its 800 kg exceeds the regulations.

od-280-s2.notes: Italian section 'Pianeta quadriciclo', A&D 280 pp.5-7. Forse il segno più eloquente: the future Fiat Multiplina (2028); European cities 'colonised' by swarms of 'senza patente' vehicles, where the Turin model could become the brand's most visible expression after the Topolino. Renault Twizy began breaking the rules over fifteen years ago with two seats in tandem; Mobilize Duo follows the same formula with glazed doors and unpainted parts, standing apart from scooters and cars. The Microlino (sketches by ICONA shown) revives the Isetta bubble car with retro-chic aesthetics, while Topolino and Multiplina miniaturise historic Fiat icons. The A-segment's disappearance (ADAS rules 2024, costs of electrification) pushes the public toward microcars, which now dare to look like real cars; Dacia Hipster, XEV Dune and Linktour Alumi show diverging takes from beach-buggy fun to technological aluminium bodies.

od-280-s3.title_en: Emotion, Made Tangible: Geely Galaxy Zhanjian 700 (Cover story)
od-280-s3.section: Emotion, Made Tangible: Geely Galaxy Zhanjian 700 (Cover story)
od-280-s3.notes: Cover story, A&D 280 pp.8-11. Geely's Galaxy TT (electric saloon, sinuous elegant lines for a young performance-minded audience) and Galaxy Zhanjian 700 (rugged SUV conveying safety, control and comfort from city to off-road) are 'two sides of the same coin'. Chen Zheng, VP Geely Auto Group and Global Design Head: 'Design is the best interpreter of a brand... form follows function, function serves experience, experience evokes emotion.' Galaxy TT takes wind as its central theme: Shark Nose front, fluid lines, active rear spoiler, 'it's the air itself that shapes the vehicle's stance', developed with aerodynamicists; cockpit inspired by an aircraft wing sweep. Zhanjian 700's strength is its vertical architecture with strong character elements such as a headlight design referencing an ancient Chinese astronomical instrument; sketches pair the front with a Chinese guardian lion. Interior materials: suede leather, Geely-developed CVU soft trim, metallic finishes, carbon-fibre-inspired textures; magnetic mounting points from dashboard to roof let equipment be clipped on.

od-275-s1.title_en: Back to Design's First Principles: Geely Galaxy Starshine 6 (Cover story)
od-275-s1.section: Back to Design's First Principles: Geely Galaxy Starshine 6 (Cover story)
od-275-s1.notes: Cover story by Edoardo Nastri, A&D 275 (Nov/Dec 2025). Thesis: after years of pronounced volumes, tall wheels and aggressive lines that sacrificed function, returning to the essence of design and precisely addressing user needs is key; Geely's principles: form follows function, design must be people-oriented and draw on culture and brand essence. Chen Zheng (VP Geely Auto Group, Global Design Head): 'Returning to first principles of user needs means creating resonance at both an emotional and a value level... provide answers to users' expectations that remain unexpressed.' Two 'manifestos': Galaxy Starshine 6 and Galaxy A7. Starshine 6's front has a large vertically developed grille for combustion-engine cooling, inspired by the power of a waterfall, with 29 sculpted elements creating visual depth and plays of light in perpetual motion; wheels evoke stars when stationary and five trails of light in motion, symbolising fortune and balance. Natural references continue in the full-width LED light bar evoking the rising sun.

od-275-s2.title_en: Geely Galaxy A7: Ripples of Galaxy (Cover story)
od-275-s2.section: Geely Galaxy A7: Ripples of Galaxy (Cover story)
od-275-s2.notes: Cover story, A&D 275. Galaxy A7 expresses the same philosophy differently: the saloon's grille is almost closed to favour aerodynamics (drag coefficient 0.22), and the full-width 'Ripples of Galaxy' light signature, 2.3 m long with 156 LEDs, references West Lake in Hangzhou; the lower headlamp section uses three hot-stamped metallic strips. Sketches show designers relied on symmetry, a full-width LED solution also replicated at the rear lamps. Six colour schemes named after nature: Enamel Blue (sky after rain), Obsidian Black (firmament at midnight), Inkstone White (race of clouds), Mist Grey (haze over river islets), Sky Ash (sky on rippling water), Frosted Silver (ice blossoms on a frozen lake). Interior draws on classical Chinese architecture and the 'Xuan' carriages for spaciousness and 'people within scenery'; panoramic roof, 27 storage compartments, 20 mm memory-foam seats; colour themes recall the seasons of West Lake; physical buttons kept for essential commands.

od-276-s1.title_en: The Aero Hatch Is Born: Hyundai THREE Concept & Art of Steel (Cover story)
od-276-s1.section: The Aero Hatch Is Born: Hyundai THREE Concept & Art of Steel (Cover story)
od-276-s1.notes: Cover story by Fabio Galvano, A&D 276. THREE (spelled out in capitals) previews the production Ioniq 3: Hyundai's first compact EV and the first car to fully adopt the new 'Art of Steel' design philosophy after previews on Ioniq 9 and Nexo. Developed at Hyundai Motor Europe under Nicola Danza (Head of Exterior Design), with Simon Loasby and SangYup Lee; Luc Donckerwolke made the final call. Danza: the philosophy is most visible 'in the lateral intersection of volumes between front and rear'; inspiration came from steel's malleability, turning its strength and flexibility into sculptural fluid volumes and precise lines. Designer Manuel Schöttle speaks of 'authenticity in the way we treated the steel'. New typology 'Aero Hatch': instead of another SUV, a hatchback reminiscent of the past with a vertical rear and strong aerodynamics; at 4.28 m long, height was masked with interplay of volumes to keep proportions. Loasby: 'a silhouette that captures a sense of fluidity and becomes a beautifully proportioned sculpture.'

od-276-s2.title_en: Hyundai THREE: from sketch to clay, Mr. Pix and yellow acrylic (Cover story)
od-276-s2.section: Hyundai THREE: from sketch to clay, Mr. Pix and yellow acrylic (Cover story)
od-276-s2.notes: Cover story process detail, A&D 276. The THREE concept was not painted but wrapped in a protective film, presenting the material 'as when it comes out of the steel mill in coils' (Danza). Yellow acrylic glass parts, coordinated with the interior and wheels, will become glass in production. Project launched September 2024: computer sketches, then a couple of 1:1 clay models to ensure the new design language and simplicity worked in three dimensions, then hard finishing. Sketches show the search for balance between soft surfaces and sharp creases at the side/rear intersection, plus aerodynamic research. 'Mr. Pix', developed with Brétécher and Danza as a humorous communication with the car, is born from the pixel graphics of the headlamps and Ioniq sub-badge (pixels linked to the Korean alphabet) and works as an Easter-egg treasure hunt; team members' names are imprinted inside the wheel arches.

od-276-s3.title_en: Little Wonders: Japan Mobility Show 2025 small cars (Design analysis)
od-276-s3.section: Little Wonders: Japan Mobility Show 2025 small cars (Design analysis)
od-276-s3.notes: Design analysis by Silvio Jr Suppa, A&D 276, Japan Mobility Show 2025. Although constrained by legal limits, the JMS remains a stage for small-format proposals and a window on how styling and vehicle types evolve; ideas start from small city cars but borrow cues from other segments. A sporty vibe dominates: Daihatsu K-Open, rounded successor to the Copen and its lineage of affordable convertibles, perfect for wind-in-the-hair fun; Honda Super One tempts orphans of the 'mini hot hatch'. Mazda Vision X-Compact breaks the barriers of the ultra-small, adds a hint of French flair, but its defining trait remains aggressive intent. Prototypes at the antipodes: Daihatsu Midget X, just 2.20 m long and 1.30 m wide, is a miniature van with a rear deck for cargo modules and lines that wink at the past, like Honda Micro EV (likely a quadricycle), while Lexus LS Micro, a self-driving single-seater, banishes retro in sharp angles. Daihatsu Kayoibako-K in bronze refutes light-transport dogmas; IMV Origin is a DIY 'chassis' for emerging markets.

od-276-s4.title_en: New Classics & Off-road in Miniature: kei cars at JMS 2025 (Design analysis)
od-276-s4.section: New Classics & Off-road in Miniature: kei cars at JMS 2025 (Design analysis)
od-276-s4.notes: Design analysis, A&D 276, Japan Mobility Show 2025. Kei cars are bound by near-draconian rules capping length at 3.40 m and width at 1.48 m, so the battle is fought on details. Suzuki Vision e-Sky concept: generous volumes and a boldly sculpted hood; Mitsubishi ek Space is impeccably well-mannered; its cousin Nissan Roox delegates its identity to a stark, technical-looking black grille; BYD Racco, a new entry from China, barely rounds off the headlights; interiors show fold-out seat-back tables and sofa-like bench seats. Off-road in miniature: when creativity is forced within legal limits, personality multiplies — Mitsubishi Delica Mini borrows the big 4WD people-mover name and now doubles down with sculpted features and off-road overtones; Daihatsu K-Vision prototype flirts more subtly with heavy-duty toughness. Chinese, full speed ahead: at EICMA Milan, Ezi EM05 and Bentu Convertible Mini EV appear as basic electric 'convertibles', perhaps future quadricycles.

od-278-s1.title_en: Car Design Award 2026: Audi, Renault and Jeep awarded (Event)
od-278-s1.section: Car Design Award 2026: Audi, Renault and Jeep awarded (Event)
od-278-s1.notes: Event report, A&D 278. The Car Design Award, founded by Auto&Design in 1984 and relaunched in 2016, held its 2026 edition with Alcantara at the ADI Design Museum during Milan Design Week (22 April). Winners: Audi Concept C (Concept Cars), Renault Twingo E-Tech Electric (Production Cars) and Jeep (Brand Design Language). Jury: Audi Concept C brought 'restored minimalism to the heart of contemporary car design, with a pure and coherent form that appears sculpted from a single block of aluminium, faithful to the marque's history whilst futuristic'; prize collected by Massimo Frascella, Chief Creative Officer Audi. Twingo transformed the small format into a genuine design statement, deftly recalling the original one-box Twingo of the 1990s (Laurens van den Acker, Renault Group). Jeep, represented by Daniele Calonaci (Head of Design Jeep Enlarged Europe), shows authenticity as the cornerstone of its creations in the energy transition. A talk 'Sustainable Intelligence – Design in the Age of AI' featured Chris Lefteri, Luca Borgogno, Florian Seidl and Alessandro Belosio (Toyota ED2). The 'Traccia' trophy by ERRE was 3D-printed using recycled coffee grounds with Lavazza and trimmed in Alcantara.

od-278-s2.title_en: Lighting Ideas: DRLs take centre stage (Design trends)
od-278-s2.section: Lighting Ideas: DRLs take centre stage (Design trends)
od-278-s2.notes: Design trends by Silvio Jr Suppa, A&D 278. One of the most significant areas of stylistic change is lighting. The two-tier lamp configuration, with roots in the 2010s, is undergoing a seismic shift: daytime running lights are shedding their supporting role to take centre stage, sometimes breaking up into graphic markers as on the Alpine A390, reducing to slim profiles, or taking the form of claws as on the Peugeot 408. The supporting role now falls to the main headlights, which on the Audi Q3 are tinted and blend into the air intakes, so the visual balance is reversed, at least by day. Further trend notes: on the Kia Vision Meta Turismo two light segments interact across hood and bumper in an open composition flowing into the windows; Lexus LS Concept makes the triangular geometry more visible; Lamborghini Manifesto completes it with a decisive downward stroke.

od-278-s3.title_en: Triangles, functional plates and aero fins in lamp design (Design trends)
od-278-s3.section: Triangles, functional plates and aero fins in lamp design (Design trends)
od-278-s3.notes: Design trends, A&D 278. Triangular suggestions: Kia Vision Meta Turismo (two light segments interacting across hood and bumper), Lexus LS Concept (more visible but unresolved geometric shape) and Lamborghini Manifesto (pattern completed with a decisive downward stroke) — a surprising evolution of a simple formula. In the name of functionality: Dacia Hipster uses simple LED-covered 'plates' without transparent diffuser because they sit behind the rear window; Citroën Oli uses square, interchangeable elements that can even become reading lamps — useful, understated, almost retro-simple responses to theatrical excesses. Aerodynamic considerations: DS N°7's two vertical blades flush with the body enclose the rear like red trim, baroque in appearance but acting as deflectors; Citroën C5 Aircross achieves the same with angular horizontal 'fins'; on Renault Twingo E-Tech Electric a small fin emerges from the tail lamps to prevent turbulence — 'the Cx sculpts the light'.

od-279-s1.title_en: A Sculpted Future: Mazda CX-6e (Cover story)
od-279-s1.section: A Sculpted Future: Mazda CX-6e (Cover story)
od-279-s1.notes: Cover story by Filippo Einaudi, A&D 279. Consistency through transformation has always marked Mazda; the CX-6e embodies its move toward electrification and a global presence. Developed with Chinese partner Changan after the Mazda 6e saloon, but unlike the 6e it introduces many new elements; designed at Mazda Motor Europe's style centre under Design Director Jo Stenuit with the Japanese team, as a global project targeting China and Europe. Stenuit: 'It was important to create a design strong enough for both markets'; Chinese customers expect a more futuristic, technological language, so the car is 'edgier, bolder and more progressive than what people normally expect from Mazda'. Proportions: a mid-to-large SUV that highlights sportiness without overstating it, inspired by European grand tourers, long bonnet, cabin tapering to the rear, almost coupé-like. Bahram Partaw, Lead Exterior Designer: 'What interests us is the feeling an object manages to generate.' The closed front with suspended light signature is the most radical Mazda has created; 'a tauter, sharper and more technological language that pushes Kodo into territories we had never ventured into'. Early sketches lacked the signature sail-shaped C-pillar, but sporty proportions were already evident.

od-279-s2.title_en: At the Intersection of Cars and Design: seamless lines & gradients (Design trends)
od-279-s2.section: At the Intersection of Cars and Design: seamless lines & gradients (Design trends)
od-279-s2.notes: Design trends by Silvio Jr Suppa, A&D 279. Ahead of the Salone del Mobile in Milan, four trends at the crossroads of mobility and home that may become leitmotifs. The unbroken line: the doors of the Velo wardrobe by Lema are free of joins or gaps around the handles, much as Cupra's experimental door panels (seen in the Cupra Raval) integrate armrest, lighting and speakers into one continuous form — 'the future is built from details, too'. The gradient effect: one colour blending softly into another, long used on walls and clothing, is entering cars thanks to new painting techniques. De Castelli's metallic Dorica furniture echoes the current Renault Clio's air vents; Megius imagines a dégradé glass shower enclosure, while the Range Rover SV Pearl of Tay has a Duotone Fade on its flanks and the Bentley Continental GT Speed Ombre by Mulliner a gradient in shades of blue.

od-279-s3.title_en: Bouclé fabric and gold finishes: home trends entering cars (Design trends)
od-279-s3.section: Bouclé fabric and gold finishes: home trends entering cars (Design trends)
od-279-s3.notes: Design trends, A&D 279. Bouclé fabric: natural fibres gain ground for ecological reasons, not necessarily 'polished' — the irregular weave draws attention back to sensory engagement, as in Cassina's Plintea and Marac's Bruna armchairs. In car interiors similar upholstery signals a genuine connection with nature plus refinement, especially in compact, reassuring modern EVs such as Kia EV2 and VW ID. Polo. Gold finishes: chrome is fading from interiors and bodies alike and 'blonde' reflections take its place. After trim details on some Mini and Alpine models, the Smart Concept #2 sports an entire straw-toned body paired with white, while the Hyundai Ioniq V evokes the sharp edges of a gold bar. In furniture, Ritmonio taps and Decor Walther accessories take on the same precious quality.
